children: The upcoming U.S.-Mexico trade talks have been rescheduled for Sept. 28-29 in Washington, D.C., delayed by a week from their original target, according to a media report on Wednesday.

While authorities haven't confirmed the exact reason for the postponement, the delay coincides with an expected visit from Chinese President Xi Jinping during the week of Sept. 21, which likely complicated scheduling for top officials, the
reported, citing people familiar with the matter.

These meetings will mark the fourth round of formal discussions aimed at updating the U.S.-Mexico-Canada Agreement, or USMCA. In these upcoming sessions, the U.S. is reportedly expected to push for stricter sourcing regulations covering artificial intelligence
Washington's main goal is to limit the percentage of components manufactured outside of North America—specifically targeting imports from China
